advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the intended semantic that a bare `transition <id> closed --force` now bypasses the completion-verification/signature close gate (previously it was discarded and the gate still ran) is desired and adequately called out for operators.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:554: `force_close=(force_reason or "(no reason given)") if force else "",` — a bare `--force` sets force_reason="" so force=True and force_close resolves to the truthy "(no reason given)"

Old parser (removed in diff): `elif a == "--force": force = True` and a separate `force_close = ""` default — a bare `--force` left force_close empty (falsy), so the close gate ran; the close path tests force_close for truthiness (transition_close.py:114 per test_llm_failure_matrix.py:517)

Commit message acknowledges the semantic change: 'on a close the valueless --force was already parsed and then discarded, so no existing invocation changes meaning except by gaining the bypass it was asking for by name.'
advisory.finding: A bare `--force` on a close transition (`transition <id> closed --force`) now BYPASSES the completion-verification/signature close gate, whereas before this change a bare `--force` on a close was parsed and discarded (force_close stayed ""/falsy) so the close gate still ran. This silently changes the behavior of an existing, previously-valid invocation form: a caller who passed a bare `--force` on a close to bypass only the start-work concept now unknowingly closes through the signature gate unsigned.
scenarios: Existing automation/operator that runs `transition <id> closed --force` (bare) expecting it to be a no-op/parsed-and-discarded flag now silently bypasses the completion-verification gate and lands the ticket closed-without-signature.
